acceptance: Decision recorded by the owner: option 1, 2 or 3, and for 1 or 2 which token
The app's actual permissions on BenchBox-dev/benchbox-site are read from its settings or installation API and recorded here before any workflow relies on them

Option 1 or 2: within one hour of a core release (trigger: core repository_dispatch on release, or a schedule no slower than hourly), a pull request into next pins the new tag via `npm run docs:pin -- <tag>` with the default fetch path, ci runs on it, and a next into main pull request exists whose body lists the docs and blog commits on next not on main

Option 2 only: merges happen only when ci concluded success for the exact head SHA, the pin pull request merges before the release pull request, the release pull request is squash-merged into main and main is then merged into next with a merge commit
Option 3: the docs-release-pending issue is assigned to the owner and its body carries the release steps from AGENTS.md in order
Every option: the issue body says which tracker items are gated on a release, and AGENTS.md says the owner unblocks them when the issue opens
Proven once end to end against a real or rehearsed release (a scratch tag on a fork, or the next real release), with the run links recorded here
AGENTS.md 'Release pin' describes the mechanism in place of the manual step
context:
Decision gates: (1) owner picks option; (2) owner approves any new permission or secret, since granting the app pull-request write widens what a core-side compromise of that app could do to the site. Guardrails: never push to main or next directly and never force-push; no bypass of the main or next rulesets; the workflow refuses a draft, prerelease or non-vX.Y.Z release and a tag whose bundle fails verification, and then leaves the issue open with the error; never use --from in automation; deploy.yml is unchanged; with option 2 a failed release pull request is reported, never retried with weaker checks. Found 2026-11-17.

2026-11-17 owner decision: option 1 (workflow pins on next by pull request and opens the next into main pull request; a person merges), token = the existing bridge app granted pull-request and contents write on benchbox-site by the owner. Design consequence found the same day: next runs ahead of each release, so the release pull request needs a human hold-back step for passages not true at the release; the workflow lists the held commits and states the steps, and never tries to hold text back itself. Implementation in progress on ci/release-docs-pr.
description:
Problem: core published v0.5.1 on 2026-11-15 and benchbox.dev still showed v0.5.0 two days later. The release process is manual by design (AGENTS.md: the owner runs docs:pin on next and opens the next into main pull request when the docs-release-pending issue appears), but the owner expected publication to follow a release, and the only signal is an unassigned issue opened by a nightly job up to a day later. The choice between manual and automatic publication was never put to the owner. Two linked gaps: the issue carries no steps and no assignee, and tracker items blocked on a release stay blocked after it (first-default-docs-pin-run and revisit-multi-warehouse-post-after-core-0-5-1 both did).

Outcome: a published core release reliably leads to a release pull request the owner can merge, or to automatic publication, as the owner decides.

Options: (1) on a new release, a workflow pins it on next by pull request and opens the next into main pull request; a person merges it. (2) as 1, plus merging both once ci is green. (3) stay manual: assign the issue to the owner and put the release steps in its body.

Constraint found 2026-11-14: a pull request opened with the default GITHUB_TOKEN never starts ci, and main and next both require ci. Options 1 and 2 need a token that can open pull requests, push to a branch and start ci: either the existing GitHub App (secrets SITE_BRIDGE_APP_ID / SITE_BRIDGE_PRIVATE_KEY) granted pull_requests and contents write on this repository, or a new fine-grained token secret. The app's current permissions were reported as contents write, issues write, actions read; that was not confirmed on the app's settings page. Repository auto-merge is off.
